text.p: Following are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thurday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President of Estonia Lennart Meri and Latvian President Guntis Ulmanis signed a joint declaration expressing determination to continue bilateral cooperation on security and defence.

- The Council of the Latvian Home Guard, including its highest commanders, has for the first time come forward with a political statement saying with resources allocated in next year's budget the Home Guard will be unable to fulfil its functions.
- Parliament has unanimously approved a statement saying the ratification of the oil licence agreement between Latvia and companies AMOCO/OPAB will be illegal.
- Latvia's Way member Ojars Kehris has been elected board chairman of the company Ventspils Nafta. Eriks Kazha representing Democratic Party Saimnieks has been elected deputy chairman of the board.
- The former deputy Prime Minister Ziedonis Chevers has been elected faction's chairman of the Democratic Party Saimnieks.

- Deputy Gundars Valdmanis as well as deputy Aleksandrs Petersons and the author of the scandalous book '10 months together with Joachim Siegerist', Maris Ruks, have asked for funds from Latvian immigrant groups to publish a weekly paper.
- Applications for the privatisation of the Latvian Shipping Company are to be submitted to the Latvian Privatisation Agency by December 20.
